sources.title: AusTender contract notices, OCDS feed (Department of Finance), as republished by the Open Contracting Partnership's Data Registry
sources.publisher: Department of Finance (AusTender); copy held by the Open Contracting Partnership
sources.notes: The Commonwealth's contract notices from 2007 to October 2026 as the AusTender API publishes them (CC BY 3.0 AU), retrieved monthly by the Open Contracting Partnership with minimal transformation; this copy was retrieved by the Partnership on 13 October 2026. AusTender's own site and data.gov.au both refuse the research crawler (robots.txt), so the full file (260 MB, sha256 27619b1bface) was read once and is not committed; the 30 records whose supplier is Palantir Technologies, and the records that mention NVIDIA, are, at data/raw/registers/open_contracting/ (filter and hash in each manifest; contact points and addresses removed, because they can name a person). Checked: the five notices read in full on AusTender in September match it value for value. Known limits, stated by the Registry: a contract's value and period are its latest after amendment, and the feed's counts can differ from the website's. No false matches on the unrelated Palantir consultancy.

sources.title: Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Cth), compilation C2026C00433, 29 September 2026
sources.notes: Section 7 and Schedule 2: the Australian Signals Directorate is an exempt agency (Part I, Division 1), and any agency is exempt in relation to a document that originated with or was received from it (s 7(2A)). The Department of Defence is exempt for documents on operational intelligence and special access programs. The ACIC and AUSTRAC are not exempt agencies; AUSTRAC intelligence documents are (s 7(2G)). ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/registers/legislation/ (sha256 4f00f6cadadc, 1,334,219 bytes).

sources.title: Privacy Impact Assessment: Overt Live Facial Recognition (WA Police Force)
sources.publisher: Western Australia Police Force, Technology Portfolio, Innovation
sources.notes: Dated November 2025 on its cover; version 1.0 of 10 May 2026. Names the vendor as NEC and the intended technology as NEC's NeoFace Watch using the NeoFace M40 algorithm, used by the Metropolitan Police; states 'Data stored in Australia' and that non-matched biometrics are not retained. Does not mention Palantir. Names three police officers, recorded here by role only. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/wapolice/ (sha256 9a8eee4abf78, 584,936 bytes); PDF not committed.

sources.title: Coles to end data analytics work with Palantir (iTnews, 4 September 2026)
sources.notes: Quotes a Coles spokesperson: 'Coles and Palantir have agreed to conclude their partnership after three years of collaboration'; timing unsettled but not expected beyond calendar 2027; the software runs in Coles' own environment and 'Palantir does not control the data'. Reports GetUp's claim of a win after 86,000 signatures. Says the Sydney Morning Herald reported it first. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/coles/.

sources.title: Coles dumps Palantir after pressure campaign (Information Age, ACS, 7 September 2026)
sources.notes: The same Coles statement, Coles' denial that Palantir had access to CCTV or facial recognition, and GetUp's email to supporters claiming the decision followed the threat of a shareholder vote. ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/coles/.

sources.title: Supermarket giant Coles to cut ties with Palantir in 2027 (Cyber Daily, 4 September 2026)
sources.notes: The same Coles statement given to Cyber Daily, and GetUp's statement, which asserts that Palantir 'still has lucrative contracts with Westpac, Rio Tinto, and a host of government agencies' (an advocacy claim, not a record of a Westpac contract). ARCHIVED 2026-10-22 at data/raw/operators/coles/.

sources.title: Coles Group 2026 Notice of Annual General Meeting

sources.title: Australian Data Centres - Western Downs Digital Park (Dexus ASX release, 16 September 2026)
sources.publisher: Dexus (ASX: DXS), distributed by EQS as a regulatory announcement of Dexus Finance Pty Limited
sources.notes: Dexus's own release, authorised by its General Counsel: Australian Data Centres (85% Dexus) holds 25% of a consortium with Zerra DC and Macquarie Capital for a hyperscale campus 'for an Australian subsidiary of Anthropic in the Western Downs region of Queensland', and the consortium 'has entered into lease documentation' for the first stage, 'subject to customary approvals'. sources.title: Transcript: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's Keynote At GTC 2025 (The Singju Post, 29 October 2025)
sources.notes: A third-party transcript of the GTC Washington, D.C. keynote of 28 October 2025, independent of Sherwood News. set.notes: Palantir announced IRAP PROTECTED completion under the Information Security Registered Assessors Program on 20 Nov 2025, assessed by an independent third-party assessor per ASD requirements. Its release states Palantir Platform Australia (PPA) delivers Foundry and AIP 'hosted in Australian Amazon Web Services (AWS) regions'. sovereign_data_carriage deliberately NULL: PPA hosting in Australian AWS regions does not establish that any specific Australian deployment (Defence CWD, ASD, ACIC, AUSTRAC) runs on PPA, and IRAP PROTECTED is an assessment level, not a sovereignty guarantee (RG-087). The certificate itself was not obtained.
